title: Berry Smoothie
subtitle: Mixed frozen berries, banana, and yoghurt blended until silky
excerpt: Frozen blueberries and strawberries blended with banana, Greek yoghurt, and milk produce a thick, deeply coloured smoothie that tastes like a dessert and costs almost nothing to make.
sourceNotes: Frozen berry smoothies are a standard weekday breakfast across British and American households; this version uses Greek yoghurt for protein and a thicker texture.

recipe.makeAheadNotes: Pre-portion berries and banana into freezer bags. Blend with yoghurt and milk straight from frozen.

content.text: Frozen berries are one of the best ingredients in a morning kitchen, always available, no prep required, and they chill the smoothie without diluting it the way ice does. This blend of {{blueberries}} blueberries and {{strawberries}} strawberries produces a colour that is almost improbably deep purple-pink, and the {{greek-yoghurt}} Greek yoghurt gives it a thick, creamy texture with real staying power. The {{banana}} banana holds everything together; without it the smoothie is thinner and slightly more acidic. Kids tend to love this one on sight.

items.prepNote: broken into chunks, fresh or frozen

content.text: Add the {{blueberries}} blueberries and {{strawberries}} strawberries to the blender jug first, frozen fruit blends best when it goes in at the bottom, closest to the blade. Add the {{banana}} banana chunks, then spoon in the {{greek-yoghurt}} Greek yoghurt. Pour in the {{whole-milk}} milk last. The liquid prevents the motor from struggling against the frozen fruit.

Blend on high for 45 to 60 seconds until completely smooth and no fruit fragments remain. Taste: most frozen berries are tart enough to need a little {{honey}} honey, especially at the beginning of the season when blueberries can be quite sharp. Add it and blend briefly if so. Pour into glasses and serve immediately.
Use coconut yoghurt and oat milk. The result is slightly less thick but just as flavourful.
A supermarket frozen mixed berry bag works well here and is usually cheaper than buying separate bags. Most contain a good mix of berry types alongside blueberries.
Stir in a tablespoon of nut butter, or add a handful of oats before blending. Both add protein and make the smoothie substantially more filling.
Halve the milk to make a very thick blend. Pour into a bowl and top with granola, sliced banana, and a drizzle of honey for a more substantial breakfast.
